payoff: AI saw where the hurricane would hit when standard forecasts didn't
means: Google's AI called Hurricane Isaias's Florida landfall when the usual physics-based models pointed elsewhere. Better track forecasts mean earlier, better-aimed evacuation warnings. It was weaker than the Hurricane Center's own forecast on how strong the storm would be.
try: Google's Weather Lab shows its AI storm forecasts live (free, Google sign-in)

payoff: OpenAI says its AI cracked three problems that stumped mathematicians and physicists for decades
means: If the claims hold, AI is starting to do original science, not just summarize it. The math proofs have been checked by computer; leading experts are now reviewing the computing and physics claims in the open.

payoff: AI now helps decide when patients are ready to go home at 12 Virginia hospitals
means: Sentara uses an AI tool to watch patients and flag who is ready to leave, across all 12 of its Virginia hospitals. That can free beds and nurses' time. The hospital group says no jobs are cut; its estimate of hours saved is still a forecast.

payoff: An AI solved 8 in 10 of medicine's hardest diagnosis puzzles. Doctors solved fewer than 4
means: On 304 of the toughest published cases, Microsoft's diagnostic AI was right 83% of the time, against 36% for general doctors, in a study in the journal Science. People with rare, hard-to-name illnesses could get answers faster. It is not available to patients yet; a hospital trial comes next.

payoff: A free map now shows every forest on Earth, down to a 10-metre patch
means: Google DeepMind's map sorts the world's forests into six types, such as natural or planted, about 90% accurately, checked at more than 9,000 sites. That makes it far harder to pass off a plantation as old forest, or to hide clearing.
try: The map is free to explore on Google Earth Engine

payoff: AI checked the code inside 123 widely used programs and found hundreds of hidden bugs
means: Anthropic says its AI mathematically checked the building blocks that many apps and websites rely on, and found defects some of which had gone unnoticed for years. Bugs like these are how hackers get in, so finding them first makes the software you use safer. This is Anthropic's own account so far.
